findings.explanation: implementation and detailedImplementation require a supported-version lookup and say 'Add the lookup and where clauses from the primary SPL', but the SPL contains no lookup or where clause; it only counts hosts by version. Description also says 'Alert logic enforces configured threshold', which the SPL does not.
findings.suggested_fix: Either add the lookup/where logic to describe unsupported versions, or reframe the UC as an inventory report and remove the alert and threshold wording.

findings.explanation: The description is built from title fragments ('Title terms: VDA, Software, and, Version, Lifecycle') and never says what a result row is: a count of machines per VDA version and OS build.
findings.quote: Surfaces when Lifecycle Tracking criteria fire for 'VDA Software and OS Version Lifecycle Tracking'
findings.suggested_fix: Describe the row grain: one row per VDA version and OS build with the number of machines and the last time each was seen, compared with supported versions.

findings.explanation: Linux boilerplate (apt/yum, nightly backup I/O, Nagios probes, load thresholds) bears no relation to a version inventory; no real cause of a wrong version row is given.
findings.suggested_fix: Use real causes: machines powered off in a catalog with stale gold-image versions, mid-rollout mixed versions, VDA version reporting differing between agent and installed build, and lab or test machines.

findings.explanation: `citrix:vda:events` and the event_type values AgentInfo, Registration and Heartbeat are not in the grounding guide's sourcetype list, and fields such as vda_version, agent_version and os_build are not documented as emitted by TA-XD7-VDA; implementation suggests the user must emit a heartbeat themselves.
findings.quote: `index=xd` `sourcetype="citrix:vda:events"` (VDA agent version, component build, plug-in status)
findings.suggested_fix: Verify the sourcetype and fields exist in TA-XD7-VDA or document exactly how to produce them (for example a scripted input reading the installed VDA version from the registry or the Broker/Monitor data).

findings.explanation: No instruction explains how to emit that event or which component produces it, so the key data feed is not actionable.
findings.quote: Emit a heartbeat or registration event at least daily that includes VDA and OS build.
findings.suggested_fix: Give the concrete collection method and fields, and a sample event.

findings.explanation: The SPL is raw-event based with no CIM fields, and the Endpoint model (processes, services, ports, filesystem) does not carry VDA agent version; an inventory-style model would fit better, or none.
findings.suggested_fix: Check whether any CIM dataset applies; if not, set cimModels to empty.

findings.explanation: The reference title promises the lifecycle matrix but the URL is the generic technical overview, so it does not support version-support claims.
findings.quote: Citrix Virtual Apps and Desktops — product matrix and lifecycle
findings.suggested_fix: Link to the Citrix product lifecycle matrix page.

firewalled_field_flags.issue: SPL has no lookup against supported versions and no `where` clause, so it cannot show unsupported VDAs as the title implies; `where vda_ver!="unknown"` is the only filter.
Compliance is claimed but the UC offers no compliance mapping; the detection is an inventory of versions.

summary: A useful idea (version inventory against a support lifecycle), but the SPL only produces a version distribution while description and implementation describe a threshold and a supported-version lookup that the SPL never uses. Prose is template-generated with Linux false positives and an unverified data source.
